# bugs #2527: mcs51: stack offsets of spill locations differ between two compilations of one file on Windows 10

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/2527/
- Category: [Already fixed in trunk](../../fixed-upstream.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as fixed in r13809, the fix for bug #3505.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The `obj.zip` of the second comment holds three sets of output files from SDCC 3.6.2 #9667, and
they show the defect. Sets 1 and 3 are equal. Set 2 differs from them only in the stack offsets of
the three spill locations of the `__reentrant` function. `sloc0`, `sloc1`, and `sloc2` have the
offsets 1, 3, and 5 in sets 1 and 3, and the offsets 4, 6, and 1 in set 2.

On r17176 the attached `win10broken.c` was compiled for mcs51 with the options of the attached
command file, `--model-small --debug -c`. In 20 compilations the `.asm`, `.adb`, `.lst`, and `.sym`
files are equal, and the `.rel` files differ only in the line that holds the output path. The
spill locations have the offsets 1, 3, and 5 each time.

The compiler under test was built on Linux, where glibc returns heap blocks in one order in every
run. To vary that order, 40 more compilations used a replacement for `malloc`, loaded through
`LD_PRELOAD`, that returns small blocks in an order chosen by a seed. Another 12 used different
values of `MALLOC_PERTURB_`. All of them gave the output of the first 20. Valgrind's memcheck
reports no error for the compiler process. No Windows build was tested.

## Fixed by

[r13809](https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/code/13809/), the fix for bug #3505, which reports code
that differs from one run to the next on macOS. `redoStackOffsets` in `src/SDCCmem.c` passes the
stack symbols of a function to `btree_add_symbol` in `src/SDCCbtree.cc`, and `btree_alloc_subtree`
assigns their offsets. Before r13809 the symbols of one block were kept in a `std::set<symbol *>`,
and the offsets followed the order of the heap addresses of the symbols. That order changes from
run to run on hosts whose allocator does not return blocks in a fixed order. r13809 replaced the
set with a `std::list<symbol *>`, which keeps the order of insertion.

The difference in the ticket is of this kind: the three spill locations belong to one block, and
only the order of their offsets changes. The code is the same for every port.

## Related

Bug #3505 is the ticket that r13809 closed.
